subject: Re: Order Form & SLA — redlines and counterproposal
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@firstbridge.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: FirstBridge Legal <legal@firstbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form + SLA redlines (FirstBridge)

Neha — attaching our marked-up Order Form and SLA. A few high-level asks so you can route internally quickly:

- We need a 99.99% uptime target for the production endpoints in the Order Form (we're running revenue-facing features).
- Service credits: 10% prorated credit for SLA misses, applied per calendar month; 15% cap? open to discussion.
- P1 response & remediation: customer expects 1 hour for acknowledgement and 4 hours for remediation (we need guarantees).
- Scheduled maintenance: we need explicit exclusions only if communicated 72 hours in advance and limited to 3 hours per maintenance window; no silent maintenance.
- Require monthly uptime reporting and right to audit incident post-mortems for Sev1 events.

Can we get a short call this week (30 min) to go over these items? Attached: FB_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf.

Thanks,
Jordan Mills

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form + SLA redlines (FirstBridge)

Jordan — thanks for the redlines and clear notes. I looped in Monica (legal) and Vivek (ops) so we can coordinate a proposal. High-level response before we set a call:

- Uptime: 99.99% is higher than our standard hosted guarantees. We can offer 99.95% for Dedicated/reserved capacity and 99.9% for Hosted API in the Order Form. If you need 99.99% we can explore a Premium Support SKU (adds reserved capacity + priority routing).
- Service credits: we typically do tiered credits (2% / 5% / 10% by severity/total monthly downtime) with a 10% monthly invoice cap. We prefer a hard cap to limit exposure.
- Response times: Ops can commit to an incident acknowledgement within 30 minutes for Sev1 and a best-effort remediation SLA (we'll propose target windows — see Vivek's note below).
- Maintenance: we will exclude scheduled maintenance when notified >=72 hours in advance and limit maintenance windows; emergency maintenance will be communicated ASAP with a follow-up post-mortem.

Options for next step: (1) 30-min sync Thursday for live negotiation, or (2) we exchange a tracked-change SLA (Monica will attach a suggested redline). I'm happy to do either.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cell: +1 (617) 555-0142

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Order Form + SLA redlines — legal suggested language

Team — quick legal analysis and proposed language we should send back. Attaching a tracked changes doc (SLA_Proposed_Track_Changes.docx). Summary of our position and proposed clauses below (short bullets to feed Neha/Jordan convo):

1) Service Availability
- Proposed: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to make the Service available 99.95% of the time per calendar month for Dedicated capacity (Order Form item) and 99.9% for Hosted API endpoints. Availability measured at the platform ingress for FirstBridge production endpoints.

2) Service Credits
- Proposed tiered credit schedule:
  * If monthly availability <99.9% and >=99.0% => credit = 2% of monthly fees attributable to impacted endpoints.
  * If monthly availability <99.0% and >=95.0% => credit = 5%.
  * If monthly availability <95.0% => credit = 10%.
- Cap credits at 10% of the monthly invoice. Credits are sole and exclusive remedy for availability.

3) Response & Escalation
- Acknowledgement: Redwood to acknowledge Sev1 incidents within 30 minutes.
- Target remediation windows: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate Sev1 incidents within 4 hours for Dedicated and 8 hours for Hosted; we should frame as "target" not a contractual availability rollback unless customer buys Premium Support.

4) Scheduled & Emergency Maintenance
- Scheduled maintenance: Redwood will provide >=72 hours notice for non-emergency maintenance and will aim to limit windows to 3 hours, scheduled outside of 0200-0600 local business hours where possible.
- Emergency maintenance: Redwood will notify customer as soon as practicable; exclude emergency maintenance from SLA calculation but require a post-incident report.

5) Reporting & Audit
- Monthly uptime report provided within 5 business days of month-end. Customer allowed to request one incident post-mortem per rolling 12 months. For additional audits, charge applies.

Recommend we propose the tracked document to Jordan, highlight the Dedicated 99.95 vs Hosted 99.9 split, and the 10% cap on credits. If Jordan insists on 99.99, we ask for Premium Support + committed capacity line item to be added to the Order Form.

--
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
Attachment: SLA_Proposed_Track_Changes.docx (docx)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA redlines — operational feasibility

Quick ops note to feed the negotiation:

- Dedicated 99.95% is feasible with reserved capacity + standard cross-region failover. For 99.99% we need: dedicated single-tenant cluster, sync-replicas across regions, and an additional premium support SLA (I'd expect a 25-40% uplift on committed spend).
- P1 handling: we can commit to 30-minute acknowledgment and a 4-hour remediation target for Dedicated (we'll escalate internally to on-call PM + Eng within 30 minutes). For Hosted, 30-minute ack / 8-hr target.
- Maintenance: ops prefers weekly maintenance windows Sunday 02:00-04:00 UTC (low traffic); we'll give 72-hour notice and limit one window per week.
- Runbooks and post-mortems: we can provide a summarized post-mortem within 5 business days; full RCA available on request (may need an NDA for some internal details).

I'll attach a short Ops_Runbook_Summary.txt with bullet points the team can share. If Jordan pushes 99.99 the cost math needs to be explicit in the Order Form (line item).

Vivek
VP of Operations, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Attachment: Ops_Runbook_Summary.txt (txt)

From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@firstbridge.ai>

Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form & SLA — counterproposal accepted with edits

Neha / Monica — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear redlines. We reviewed the tracked changes and internal ops constraints. FirstBridge is willing to accept the following compromise so we can move to signature:

- Availability: 99.95% for the Dedicated capacity listed on the Order Form; 99.9% for Hosted API.
- Service credits: agree to the tiered schedule as outlined by Monica, with a monthly cap of 10%.
- Response & remediation: accept 30-minute acknowledgement; agree to the remediation target windows (4 hours Dedicated, 8 hours Hosted) as "target" windows.
- Maintenance: accept 72-hour notice for scheduled maintenance; require the post-incident report for emergency maintenance.

We will sign the Order Form with those edits and will execute via DocuSign. Sending our final sign-off and DocuSign envelope now: https://docusign.com/complete?envelopeId=0a1b2c3d

Please confirm once the Order Form is countersigned on your side and whether the MSA needs an additional signature page or a route through Legal.

Jordan Mills
